_about: Component spec for pos-badge — created 2026-10-06 from the approved component-wizard draft (Figma node 8293:129201) via scripts/generate-component.js. Single source of truth for the Variants/Usage/Tokens tabs on /style-guide. Six variants: type (dot / number / max-count) × size (small / big); not interactive, so only the normal state. Figma names looked up in tokens/css-to-figma.json (RULES.md §6.4). Regenerate spec-badge.liquid after any change here — never hand-edit the .liquid partial.
name: Badge
description: A small, round indicator on another element — a dot for "something new", or a count (up to 9, then "99+"), in an intent color (important by default) with a ring in the background color that separates it from what it sits on.
whenToUse: Signaling that something new is waiting on an icon or avatar — a dot, no number (e.g. new messages on a bell).
Showing a small unread / pending count on an icon or tab — a number, or the max-count "99+" form when it gets large.
whenNotToUse: The information is a status or category with words — use a Tag or a Chip.
The message is important enough that the user must not miss it — use an Alert card or a Toast; a badge is a quiet, glanceable supplement.
The label would need more than a few characters — badges hold a dot, a number or "99+" only.
do: Place the badge at the top-right corner of the element it belongs to, overlapping its edge.
Switch to the max-count form above 99 ("99+") so the badge never grows wide.
Use the small size on small icons (16px) and the big size on larger icons, avatars or tabs.
dont: Make the badge itself clickable — it describes its anchor element, which is the interactive part.
Put more than one badge on the same element.
Use a badge for status words or long text.
accessibility: The badge is visual only: put the meaning into the anchor's accessible name (e.g. aria-label="Notifications, 3 unread") — screen readers don't announce a bare number in context.
A dot badge has no text: mark it aria-hidden="true" and say "new" in the anchor's label.
The white (background-colored) ring keeps the badge visible on any background — don't remove it.

props.name: type
props.description: Dot: no content, aria-hidden. Number: one digit (1–9). Max count: a short count like "99+", the badge widens with padding.

props.name: intent
props.description: Fill color by meaning: important (alerts, unread), confirmation (done, online), brand (highlight in the brand color), neutral (low-emphasis, grey).

usageExample: 9 99+ 3 99+
